setup.title: Initial setup
setup.subtitle: A few settings and the desk is ready to work.
setup.alreadyRun: You have already been through this wizard. You can come back to it at any time via /setup.
setup.appearanceLead: This choice is yours, not the tenant’s: every agent keeps their own. The theme is shared with the other applications in the suite.
setup.appearanceNote: French and English ship with the product. The suite’s other languages exist but are not translated for this desk yet.
setup.baselineDetail: Shipped: the General, Network, Security and Integration queues; the Business hours and 24×7 calendars; the Standard SLA policy; five views in the sidebar; the default lifecycle.
setup.baselineLead: Your desk already works. This wizard tunes a shipped configuration, it does not build one.
setup.demoItemConfig: A copy of this tenant’s published configuration: queues, SLAs, calendars, views, lifecycle.
setup.demoItemSafe: Nothing is written into your current tenant.
setup.demoItemTickets: Tickets spread across the queues, with varied impact and urgency (priority is computed by the real matrix) and occurrence dates spread over 30 days.
setup.demoLead: You cannot judge a queue, its virtualisation, an SLA chip or collision detection with zero tickets. This step creates some, in a separate tenant, and knows how to wipe them all.
setup.demoNeedsAdmin: Creating or deleting a tenant requires a platform administrator role.
setup.demoPurgeExplain: The purge deletes the tenant and everything in it: tickets, journal, SLAs, mail, audit log. There is no undo. Your working tenant is untouched.
setup.demoTicketBody: Demonstration ticket created by the getting-started wizard. Delete the “Demonstration” tenant to wipe everything.
setup.identityLead: The name shown everywhere, the ticket number prefix, and the tenant’s reference time zone.
setup.identityNeedsAdmin: Editing the tenant requires an administrator role. You can skip this step; an administrator will pick it up from Settings › General.
setup.leave: Leave without losing anything already saved
setup.mailLead: Optional. The desk works without e-mail: tickets then arrive through the portal, the API, or direct entry.
setup.orgSlugHint: Cannot be changed: every application in the suite knows you by this slug.
setup.pollSecondsHint: An installation setting, not a tenant one: it holds for every organisation hosted here. Between 15 and 3600.
setup.portalEnabledHint: Requesters see their own tickets and can reply, with no access to the desk.
setup.queueDefaultHint: Any ticket with no explicit queue lands here. The former default queue is demoted at the same time.
setup.queueDemoteFailed: The former default queue could not be demoted.
setup.queueGroupHint: The shipped group is “service-desk” and contains the administrator. The groups themselves are managed in Administration › Configuration.
setup.queueGroupSlug: Slug of the group that receives these tickets
setup.queueLead: Four queues are already in service. Rename one to match your vocabulary, or add your own.
setup.queuePublishNote: Publishing goes through the linter: a reference that points at nothing is refused with the detail, not silently accepted.
setup.queueSlugHint: Lower case, digits, hyphen and underscore.
setup.queueSlugLocked: The slug is the queue’s identity: it is not renamed.
setup.slaHolidays: The fixed-date French public holidays are already in place. The movable ones (Easter Monday, Ascension, Whit Monday) are deliberately absent rather than wrong: add them under SLAs and teams.
setup.slaLead: SLA durations are counted in business minutes on the chosen calendar: “1 day” is 540 minutes from 09:00 to 18:00, not 1440.
setup.slaMinutesNote: Values in business minutes. An empty or zero field is ignored: the shipped target stays in place rather than becoming impossible to meet.
setup.smtpForbidden: SMTP server management exists on this server but your account has no access to it.
setup.smtpMissing: The HTTP surface for SMTP servers is not mounted in this build: the service exists, the route is not exposed yet. Nothing to configure here for now.
setup.stripQuoted: Strip the quoted history from replies
setup.stripQuotedHint: Without this, every reply copies the whole thread into the journal and makes it unreadable after three exchanges.
setup.ticketPrefixHint: Numbers already issued keep their old prefix.

finding.allActionsDisabled: Every action is disabled: the rule will run for nothing.
finding.nameRequired: Without a readable name, the ordered list stops being readable.
finding.noAction: A rule with no action can match, but will do nothing.
finding.noTrigger: A rule with no trigger will never be evaluated.
finding.scheduleEmpty: A scheduled trigger needs an interval in minutes or a cron expression.
finding.slugRequired: A rule needs an identifier (slug): everything references it by that.
finding.slugShape: The slug accepts lower case, digits, hyphen and underscore, starting with a letter or a digit.

rules.guardrails: Engine guardrails: {{budget}} actions per ticket per event, re-entry depth {{depth}}, circuit breaker after {{threshold}} consecutive failures.
rules.identityHelp: The slug is the identifier everything references this rule by: execution log, decisions, exports. It cannot be renamed after publication.
rules.lintBlocked: Publication refused: see the findings above.
rules.lintRefused: The configuration check refused this publication

log.dryRunHelp: A dry run describes what WOULD have happened. This log is the record of what the desk did: the two do not mix.
log.emptyDesc: The engine writes one line per rule per event, whether it matched or not. Nothing here means no event has reached these rules with these filters yet.
log.noEntries: No detail recorded for this execution.

rules.name: Readable name
rules.neverRan: Never ran over the observed period
rules.newRuleHint: It will be created, linted, then published.

rules.positionHelp: Execution order: rules apply top to bottom.

rules.sharedHelp: Pushed from the master tenant: editable only there.

rules.simulateHelp: Replays your latest real tickets through the production engine, writing nothing.

rules.simulationFailed: The dry run did not complete
rules.simulationFooter: Trigger “{{trigger}}”, sample of {{sample}} tickets, {{ms}} ms. Nothing written: every replay runs in a rolled-back transaction.

skip.alreadyRan: Already ran once on this ticket

rules.whenHelp: Evaluated by the same engine on both sides of the wire. An empty condition means “always”.
